region.text: Calatrava and the Campo de Calatrava

ledger.note: 1157: the abbey's lay brothers, on Father Diego Velázquez's idea, become soldiers of the Cross and the Order of Calatrava is created. 'Thus a new order was created in 1157.' Calatrava had been 'recovered from the Muslims, in 1147, by the King of Castile, Alfonso VII'; the Campo page: 'founded in 1158 to defend the fortress of Calatrava'. The page says the Order 'enjoyed autonomy, being by its constitutions independent in temporal matters'.
1179: the Aragonese branch is founded: 'a new encomienda (landed estate), that of Alcañiz (1179)'. The granting king is not named; the Crown of Aragon is the reading.

region.text: Calatrava and the whole Campo, lost after Alarcos

ledger.note: 1195: after the defeat at Alarcos the knights 'abandoned their bulwark of Calatrava to the Almohads (1195)'; the Campo page: the Order lost 'its stronghold and the whole Campo to the Almohads'.
1198: the Order raises Salvatierra Castle: 'They soon erected a new bulwark, Salvatierra Castle, where they took the name.' Salvatierra fell to the Almohads in 1209; as one fortress it is not drawn.

region.text: Calatrava and the Campo, retaken in the campaign of Las Navas de Tolosa

ledger.note: 1212: 'An early battle was the reconquest of Calatrava (1212), which was returned to its former masters'; the Campo page has the Christian army seize the Campo on its way south, with Dueñas and Salvatierra excepted.

1218: the seat moves to Calatrava la Nueva: the Order 'removed to more secure quarters of Calatrava la Nueva' (the Order page lists the Order resuming the name of Calatrava in 1216 and moving in 1218; the Campo page says 'towards 1214').

region.text: the Order of Monfragüe, merged into Calatrava

ledger.note: 1221: 'In 1221 the Order of Monfragüe was merged into that of Calatrava.' The page does not locate its lands.

region.text: the Order's lordships, whose political autonomy ended

ledger.note: 1487: Ferdinand presents 'a Bull from Innocent VIII that invested him with authority to administer the order'; 'Thus ended the political autonomy of the Order of Calatrava.' The estates remained the Order's until the secularisation of 1838 (page).

region.text: the Order's lordships, administered by the Crown

ledger.note: 1487: the Order of Calatrava ends as a political body; the Crown of Castile administers it.

wars.name: Battle of Alarcos
wars.outcome: An Almohad victory: the Order abandoned Calatrava (1195) and with it the Campo.

wars.name: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
wars.outcome: Christian victory: Calatrava reconquered in 1212 and returned to the Order; Dueñas and Salvatierra excepted.

certainty.note: Scattered lordships, not a bordered state: the pages give commanderies and villages, no boundary; the circles are readings.

sources.title: Order of Calatrava
sources.note: Creation 1157, 1164 bull, Alcañiz 1179, Alarcos 1195, Salvatierra 1198-1209, Las Navas 1212, Calatrava la Nueva 1218, Monfragüe 1221, 1487 administration, 64 villages and 56 commanderies; no area.

sources.title: Campo de Calatrava
sources.note: Founded 1158; lost the whole Campo in 1195, seized in 1212, seat moved c. 1214; no lordship extent.

notes: Written for eu-12-x (the group scope names the military orders' lands); two pages. Cliopatria has no row for any military order; the Campo is inside its Kingdom of Castile shapes. The Order is typed a state because the page says it 'enjoyed autonomy, being by its constitutions independent in temporal matters'; it is not an independent sovereign, so the rendering may prefer the vassal tint of the Crown of Castile. Not done: the Order of Santiago, Alcántara, Montesa, Avis/Christ and the Templars and Hospitallers: the Santiago page (opened) lists headquarters and provinces (Segura de la Sierra, Segura de León, Mérida, Llerena) but dates no territorial acquisition, so no dossier was written (see report gaps). Not settled: the Campo's extent (the 35 km circle covers roughly the Campo; Ciudad Real province would overstate it); the Order's seat between 1195 and 1198 and 1209-1218; where Salvatierra and Monfragüe lay; whether Alcañiz was held 1195-1211. Capitals are approximate: all three seats are drawn at the Ciudad Real coordinates because the gazetteer lacks Calatrava. Gazetteer names needed: Ciudad Real, Alcañiz, Monfragüe (places). Dates differ across pages: creation 1157 (Order) or 1158 (Campo); move to Calatrava la Nueva 1218 (Order) or c. 1214 (Campo); dissolution of property 1838 (Order page; not 1835).
